subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat `all | final | off` tool-error delivery policy beyond the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` boolean, and what should it do when a mutating tool failed but the final reply looks successful?
rationale: This changes user-visible failure delivery and config surface: it can reduce confusing hosted/team-chat warning bubbles, but it can also hide real failed mutations that current main intentionally surfaces.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default plus explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove unresolved failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep the boolean only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator opt-out and narrow this issue to docs or specific remaining leak bugs.

options.title: Split narrow leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and handle warning order, Feishu leakage, exec detail behavior, and lifecycle routing in their existing narrower issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default plus explicit `final` and/or `off` modes after tests prove unresolved failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged warning-policy PR explicitly left this issue open for the broader delivery-policy decision.
